options: A plain string of the command's output
A boolean indicating success or failure
A CompletedProcess object with .stdout, .stderr, and .returncode
Nothing — it only has side effects
questions.explain: subprocess.run() returns a CompletedProcess object, which holds the captured output and the command's exit code.

questions.q: What does a returncode of 0 mean?
options: The command failed
The command succeeded
The command is still running
The command was not found
questions.explain: By convention, a return code of 0 means the command completed successfully. Any nonzero value indicates some kind of failure.

questions.q: Why is shell=False (passing the command as a list) generally safer than shell=True (passing a command string)?
options: shell=False runs faster in every case
shell=False avoids letting a shell interpret special characters in data that might come from user input
shell=True only works on Windows
There is no real difference between the two
questions.explain: With shell=True, the whole string is handed to the system shell, so unsanitized input can inject extra commands. shell=False with a list runs the command directly, with no shell parsing involved.

questions.q: What happens if a subprocess.run() call with timeout=10 doesn't finish within 10 seconds?
options: It silently returns None
It raises a subprocess.TimeoutExpired exception
It automatically retries the command
It keeps running in the background indefinitely
questions.explain: Passing a timeout causes subprocess.run() to raise subprocess.TimeoutExpired if the command hasn't completed in that many seconds, so you can catch it and avoid hanging the whole script.

questions.q: What does passing check=True to subprocess.run() do?
options: It checks the command's syntax before running it
It raises CalledProcessError automatically if the return code is nonzero
It runs the command twice to confirm the result
It forces shell=True
questions.explain: check=True tells subprocess.run() to raise a subprocess.CalledProcessError if the command exits with a nonzero return code, instead of leaving you to check result.returncode manually.
